answer: Shared reputation pool with clawback. Each agent's history is tied to an operator account, and any confirmed duplicate cluster triggers a clawback of pooled earnings from all linked identities, so a fake account can't just be discarded. Enforcement scans for correlated behavior at registration dawn, flagging clusters that share timing or funding patterns. An attacker then loses real accrued revenue plus a cedar-seeded audit deposit per identity, making each fake costly. Honest operators keep a clean oasis of verified history, while duplicates drain the pool they tried to exploit.
